combos.label: Solution A
combos.title: Interior progression
combos.objective: Create a free player by attracting the first pressure and connecting through an interior support or third-man action.
principles: Numerical superiority in the first line
key_actions: Use the goalkeeper as an active build-up player when the press commits forward.
Keep supporting angles staggered instead of forming flat passing lines.
Fix the nearest presser before releasing the next receiver.
Accelerate after the free player receives facing forward.
risk_notes: Central losses can expose the team before rest defence is organised.
The receiver must scan early because pressure can arrive from the blind side.
coaching_points: Create distance before asking for the ball.
Receive with an open body whenever possible.
Do not force the vertical pass before the opponent is fixed.

combos.label: Solution B
combos.title: Outside release
combos.objective: Manipulate the press centrally and use width to escape through the outside lane with a safer first progression.
key_actions: Invite pressure toward one side before changing the exit lane.
Keep the wide outlet available at a useful receiving height.
Support the first wide receiver with an inside option and a return pass.
Progress only when the opponent's block has been displaced.
risk_notes: A slow switch can allow the opponent to trap the receiver near the touchline.
Excessive width without interior support can isolate the first receiver.
coaching_points: Recognise when the central lane is intentionally closed.
Play away from pressure, not simply toward the touchline.
Keep the next pass prepared before the wide reception.

combos.label: Solution A
combos.title: Goalkeeper + third-man press escape
combos.objective: Use the goalkeeper to create first-line superiority, attract the 4-2-3-1 press and free a technically strong midfielder for the next progression.
key_actions: Use the goalkeeper to force the first pressing line to choose a reference.
Create a passing angle that prevents the two central midfielders from being screened simultaneously.
Use a third-man connection when the direct central receiver is locked.
Accelerate once the free midfielder receives beyond the first pressure.
risk_notes: The central turnover is dangerous if the rest-defence structure is not prepared.
Spacing must be large enough to stretch the press but short enough to protect the next pass.
coaching_points: Do not bypass the goalkeeper if the extra player can move the press.
Fix one opponent before releasing the next player.
The third-man receiver should already know the forward option before receiving.

combos.label: Finishing Pattern
combos.title: Coordinated final-third occupation
combos.objective: Coordinate occupation of the box and supporting zones so the final action has multiple references instead of a single target.
key_actions: Attack different finishing lanes rather than the same space.
Keep one support player available outside the immediate finishing line.
Coordinate near-side, central and far-side arrivals.
Maintain balance for the second action if the first finish is blocked.
risk_notes: Too many simultaneous runs can empty the support zone behind the ball.
Poor rest defence can expose the team after a blocked cross or shot.
coaching_points: Arrive at different times and heights.
Attack space, not only the ball.
Protect the next action while committing players to finish.
